text:
maya: Heads-up: after enabling cross-warp coalescing + prefetch in the Flash variant (kvwave branch) we see a ~8% throughput drop on medium seqs (512-1024) with KV cache enabled. Noticed higher L2 stall and SM idle in profiler.

sam: Hmm, 8% is annoying but small. Is this consistent across GPUs? A100 and H100?

maya: Quick summary: A100 (prod-canary) shows drop, H100 less pronounced. Repro script attached below. Kernel that spikes is `flash_coalesce_prefetch_kernel` (name from our patch).

lucas: Can you paste the nsys output snippet? curious about mem bw utilization + smem per-block.

maya: Sure. Ran: `nsys profile -o /tmp/kvwave --trace=cuda,kernels --force-overwrite --sample=none ./bin/bench_kvwave`

```
GPU: 0 A100-SXM4-40GB
Kernel: flash_coalesce_prefetch_kernel
Avg SM Util: 62%  (down from 78% on baseline)
L2 BW: 210 GB/s (baseline 280 GB/s)
DRAM BW: 520 GB/s (baseline 540 GB/s)
SMEM per-block: 48 KB
Concurrent blocks/SM: 2
```

maya: nvprof counters show high `stall_inst_executing` and `pipe_alu_idle`.

jin: That smells like high shared-memory pressure -> fewer blocks per SM. Coalescing improved per-warp mem pattern but increased smem scratch per-block for prefetch buffer, so occupancy dropped.

lucas: If concurrent blocks/SM is 2, that's probably the cause. Baseline was 4 blocks/SM, right? We should try reducing per-thread smem allocation or split prefetch buffer across iterations.

sam: Another angle: maybe L2 prefetch changed traffic pattern causing more L2 thrash for medium seqs where KV cache hits are common. Could be cross-warp prefetches evict hot KV entries.

ana (typo correction): I mean ana: We should test with KV pinned vs unpinned. If prefetch evicts KV pages, pinning should show improvement. Also try smaller prefetch distance for seq=512.

maya: Ran quick microbench across seq lengths. Script: `scripts/bench_tokens.sh --variant kvwave --batch 8 --warm 50 --iter 200`

```
seq, tokens/s (baseline), tokens/s (kvwave)
128, 21000, 21500
256, 18500, 18800
512, 15200, 14100  <-- regression
1024, 12400, 12100
```

maya: So regression concentrated around 512.

jin: Can you try toggling `warp_coalesce` flag at runtime? If setting it off restores baseline, we can gate it behind a heuristic keyed to seq length + kv-cache-hit-rate.

maya: I tried: `--warp-coalesce=0` on same run -> tokens/s for 512 becomes 15150 (almost baseline).

lucas: That confirms it's our coalescing prefetch path. Two mitigation ideas: 1) dynamic heuristic (disable coalesce when KV cache hit-rate > X and seq in mid-range), 2) reduce per-block smem (move some buffers to registers or use double-buffering streaming across iterations).

sam: For (1) we can add a quick router-level probe: sample the last 100 requests for hit-rate and seq distribution, then pick kernel variant per-request. Low cost to implement and should avoid regression for most apps.

ana (ana): For (2) please check if we can quantize the prefetch index structure to 16-bit to halve smem footprint. If correctness holds that's an easy win.

ops-bot: deploy-canary: started canary job kvwave-coalesce-fallback @ maya/sam. Job id 74234. Logs: https://ci/redwood/74234

maya: Also saw increased L2 read streams when coalescing on - likely more concurrent small reads instead of fewer large reads. That hurts our L2 efficiency for medium seqs.

lucas: Another knob: increase tile width so each warp covers more keys -> fewer cross-warp prefetches. But that may increase register pressure. Need microbenchmark tradeoff.

sam: Action items: maya -> collect nsys traces for pinned KV vs unpinned for seq=512; lucas -> experiment reducing smem by 2x (try 16-bit indices); jin -> implement a simple runtime heuristic flag gated by seq range and kv_hit_rate; ana -> run tile-width sweep across 256/512/1024 on A100.

maya: I'll attach the lightweight trace here (shortened):

```
Timeline: strong L2 read concurrency at flash_coalesce_prefetch_kernel
SM occupancy drops when smem > 40KB
Prefetch distance=4 causes more L2 lines fetched per token
```

jin: For the runtime heuristic I propose: if kv_hit_rate > 0.6 AND seq in [400,800] then use fallback kernel. Keep sampling window 100 requests, rate limit switches to 1 per 30s. Low overhead.

sam: Sounds reasonable. Add a metric (coalesce_fallback_count) to console for visibility.

ana (ana): I'll try the 16-bit index change. If it reduces smem and keeps correctness, we can enable it by default.

maya: Can we also add a canary that routes 10% of traffic to kvwave with coalesce enabled vs 90% fallback to measure real-world impact? ops-bot, can you set up a canary split?

ops-bot: deploy-canary: created traffic-split kvwave-coalesce 10% on prod-canary. Start in 10m.

lucas: One more check: ensure L2 cache allocation settings (cuda l2) not different between builds; sometimes link-time flags affect usable L2. But since baseline and kvwave built same night, unlikely. Still worth double-checking.

maya: OK let's reconvene after individual tasks. I'll post nsys tarball and microbench script to the thread when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: Cool. If fallback heuristic looks stable we can ship as hotfix and iterate on smem reduction later.

lucas: Agreed. Small runtime guard + telemetry is fastest path to mitigate customer-facing regressions.

maya: I'll open an RFC PR with results + perf numbers and assign owners. Will link here.

ops-bot: jira: created PERF-1384 "kvwave cross-warp coalesce regression investigation" assigned maya/lucas/jin/ana.

maya: end of thread for now.
